acceptance: Website, README, MCP registry, installer, and Hub show the same support tier.
observed: tools/productization/generate-support-matrix.mjs is the single generator for the support-tier matrix and is the only writer of every surface this task's allowlist covers: docs/support-matrix.md, docs/support-matrix.json, the <!-- support-matrix:start/end --> block in README.md, and the per-target nativeArtifacts[*].platformReceipt fields in server.json (the MCP Registry server descriptor consumed by MBR-907's registry publication). All four are computed from one buildMatrix() call over the same real MBR-801 conformance receipts in a single generate() run, so they cannot drift relative to each other by construction: docs/support-matrix.json is the machine-readable canonical source, docs/support-matrix.md and the README block are its human-readable renderings, and server.json's platformReceipt fields are the same receipt data reshaped for the registry descriptor. The website (website/**) and Hub (apps/membrane-hub/**) surfaces named in the acceptance criterion are out of this task's allowlist (apps/membrane-hub/** is reserved by a concurrent lane per this task's explicit instructions) and are not modified here; docs/support-matrix.json is the intended single canonical artifact those surfaces will read from once their own tasks wire them up, and this generator's existence and tests demonstrate the derivation mechanism they will consume. The installer surface does not yet exist in this repository (MBR-901/902/903 are undone Wave-3 tasks) and could not fabricate a tier without inventing an installer. The deterministic test suite (10/10 passing) proves the never-fabricate contract directly: buildMatrix() renders `unavailable` for every platform/client pair when no receipt exists, when no current release generation is supplied even with a receipt present, when a receipt names a stale commit, and when a receipt's scenario coverage is incomplete despite an otherwise well-formed file; it renders `qualified` only for the exact (platform, client) pair a current, fully verified MBR-801 receipt names, never for a sibling client or the other platform. applyServerJson() is proved to only ever populate a target's platformReceipt when that target's platform is currently qualified. Running the real generator against the actual working tree (node tools/productization/generate-support-matrix.mjs, logged in commands.log) confirms all ten rows currently, honestly render `unavailable` with reason 'no current commit/release-generation to verify against (release evidence not yet published)' — the true current state, since no MBR-807/903 release evidence and no evidence/qualification/mbr801/** receipt exist yet in this repository — and that a second run of the generator is byte-idempotent, including leaving server.json completely untouched because applying the (unchanged) matrix produces no semantic difference.
deferredWork: Real conformance data: an actual evidence/qualification/mbr801/<platform>/receipt.json (from MBR-801's harness, itself deferred to the Book 2 gate) and a real release-evidence manifest (from MBR-807/903, undone Wave-3 tasks) do not exist yet in this repository. Wiring the website and Hub surfaces named in the acceptance criterion to docs/support-matrix.json is out of this task's allowlist (website/** is not listed; apps/membrane-hub/** is explicitly reserved by a concurrent lane) and belongs to those surfaces' own tasks. This task does not claim acceptance pass and does not execute the manifest command node scripts/qualification/run.mjs --task MBR-808 — that command does not implement MBR-808 in the first place; it is MBR-801's harness entrypoint, which this generator only reads finished evidence from.
